title: Adaptive Workspace Lens & Routing — cost-focused console zones
creator: Jonah Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket proposes a new information architecture pattern for the Redwood Console that replaces dense, mode-based sidebar navigation with an "Adaptive Workspace Lens". The Lens is a contextual, zone-based router that surfaces task-relevant routes, an inline cost-metrics panel, and quick workspace actions. The objective is to reduce navigation friction for engineers and platform teams while surfacing per-route cost impact and rollout controls earlier in user flows.

Problem statement:
- Users currently need 3–4 clicks to reach the most common console destinations (model routes, rollouts, billing breakdowns).
- Cost telemetry and rollout controls sit in separate surfaces, causing cognitive context switches during incident triage and performance tuning.
- Newer features (rollouts, canaries, cost breakdowns) are not discoverable from common workflows.

Goals and constraints:
- Reduce mean time-to-action for: checking model route health, toggling canary rollouts, and viewing cost deltas for recent traffic changes.
- Maintain keyboard-first navigation and accessible semantics (WCAG AA).
- Keep per-route latency/throughput panels visible without forcing full route navigation.
- Low engineering risk for initial rollout: phase work to require minimal backend changes in Phase 1.

Proposed changes (high level):
1) Adaptive Workspace Lens: a compact, horizontally collapsible lens at the top-left that replaces the static left rail. It exposes 3 contextual rows: Global Lenses (Workspaces, Projects), Active Routes (quick open for routes recently used by the user), and Actions (rollout control, cost snapshot, open trace).
2) Zone routing model: map routes into lightweight "zones" (Observe, Tune, Deploy, Cost) so users can jump into a behavioral surface instead of a single destination. Zones are shallow: clicking a zone provides quick filters and a list of related entities.
3) Inline Cost Panel: a persistent, collapsible cost strip that lives alongside the route list with per-route 24h/7d cost deltas and token-level breakdowns. Clicking the metric expands a compact dashboard for deeper investigation.
4) Workspace quick-switch: single-component switcher with fuzzy search + recently-used pins + workspace role indicator; integrates with Lens to preserve context when switching.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- We trade some discoverability of deep items for speed of common tasks; to mitigate we include an always-available command palette.
- The Lens uses progressive disclosure to avoid overwhelming new users; advanced toggles hidden under an "Advanced" expansion.
- Inline cost panel initially shows aggregated, precomputed deltas to avoid perf overhead; full token-level rollups available behind a "Drill into Billing" action that hits analytics endpoints.

Accessibility and keyboard flow:
- All Lens elements follow roving tabindex and aria-activedescendant patterns.
- Zone keyboard shortcuts planned: Ctrl+1..4 to jump to Observe/Tune/Deploy/Cost.

Phased rollout plan:
Phase 1 (minimal backend): implement Lens UI, Zone routing shell, workspace switcher, and cost strip with cached deltas. Toggle behind feature flag for 10% of orgs.
Phase 2 (data integrations): enable live per-token breakdowns, integrate Console tracing links with Lens actions, add rollback shortcuts.
Phase 3 (full rollout): move to default for all new orgs and opt-in for existing orgs after telemetry review.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in clicks-to-rollout or clicks-to-cost-inspection in pilot orgs.
- Increase in usage of rollout canary toggles by 30% for teams exposed to Lens.
- No regression in keyboard accessibility scores; automated a11y tests pass.

Open questions for engineering:
- Can cached cost deltas be computed as part of nightly jobs or do we need a near-real-time stream?
- What limits should we place on inline dashboard queries to avoid adding load?

Deliverables and artifacts:
- Figma prototype (see attachments) with full keyboard flow and micro-interactions.
- High-level PRD in Drive linking backend contract proposals.
- Usability test script for the pilot cohort.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for Phase 1):
- Contextual prompts to suggest model quantization or batching settings when cost spikes are detected.
- Rollout A/B tracking directly surfaced in the Lens.

Next steps — Deliver final redlines, handoff to ENG-5650 for implementation of Lens interactions and keyboard bindings. Schedule pilot with two internal orgs (Platform team, Data infra).
